strings.GameSettings.VirtualFolders.Information:
[Virtual Install] This is the default and recommended installation method. It REQUIRES this folder to be located on the same hard-drive where you normally install mods for this game.
If you want this folder to be located anywhere, on any hard-drive of your choosing, enable the Multi-HD install mode.




[Enable Multi-HD install mode] lets you place extracted mods on a different hard-drive to the one your game mods are usually installed on,allowing you to save space on your game drive.
NOTE: Some file extensions like .exe, .esp and .esm files need to be placed on the game's hard-drive irrespsective of this setting.
NOTE: Placing mods on a slow HD may degrade game performance and loading times.


[Required Link] Select the folder where NMM will place extracted files that need to be on the same HD as your games (.exe, .esp and .esm files)
NOTE: This folder MUST be on the same HD where you normally install mods for this game.

NMM found an old install-log setup for this game mode.

The legacy migration tool used to reinstall or uninstall every active mod automatically. That process is no longer run at startup because it can remove working files without enough user control.

Detected active install-log entries: {0}
Virtual install folder: {1}

NMM will keep the existing files in place. Some profile and virtual-install features may not work correctly until this setup is repaired manually.

Recommended recovery path:
1. Back up the game folder, NMM config folder, and mod archives.
2. Verify that the Mods folder and Virtual Install folder in Settings point to the correct locations.
3. Reinstall or reactivate the affected mods manually once the folders are correct.

strings.Mods.CacheMigration.Message:
This new version changes the way NMM handles its cache. This update is designed to make NMM load faster. As a result the old caching system is no longer necessary. 

This prompt is here to ask you what you would like to do with the files on your hard-drive used by NMM for the old caching system. We estimate this system used around 1MB - 100MB of space on your hard-drive, depending on how many mods you have installed in NMM. 

If you select 'Yes' then NMM will delete the old cache files and do some spring cleaning. This will free up the small amount of space being used, but if you switch back to a previous version of NMM from before this update it will take a long time to recreate the cache again. 

If you select 'No' then NMM will not delete the old cache files and they will remain on your hard-drive. The only negative to this, as mentioned, is the fact it'll take up a little extra space on your hard-drive (once again, estimated at 1MB to 100MB of space). 

Would you like NMM to remove your old cache files?

strings.Startup.Initialization.WritePermission.G:
This error happens when you are running Windows Vista or later, and have installed {0} in the Program Files folder. You need to do one of the following:
  1. Disable UAC (not recommended).
  2. Move {0} outside of the Program Files folder (for example, to C:\Games\{0}). This may require a reinstall.
    With Oblivion you could just copy the game folder to a new location, run the game, and all would be well. This may not work with other games.
  3. Run {1} as administrator. You can try this by right-clicking on {1} shortcut and selecting Run as administrator. Alternatively, right-click on the shortcut, select Properties->Compatibility and check Run this program as an administrator.
The best thing to do in order to avoid other problems, and the generally recommended solution, is to install {0} outside of the Program Files folder.

strings.Startup.Initialization.WritePermission.N:
This error happens when you are running Windows Vista or later, and have put {0}'s {1} folder in the Program Files folder. You need to do one of the following:
  1. Disable UAC (not recommended).
  2. Move {0}'s {1} folder outside of the Program Files folder (for example, to C:\Games\ModManagerInfo\{1}).
  3. Run {0} as administrator. You can try this by right-clicking on {0}'s shortcut and selecting Run as administrator. Alternatively, right-click on the shortcut, select Properties->Compatibility and check Run this program as an administrator.
The best thing to do in order to avoid other problems, and the generally recommended solution, is to Move {0}'s {1} folder outside of the Program Files folder.
